newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures slipped from a new contract high set earlier in the session after fears of a U.S. rate rise next week sent U.S. bond prices lower.
Earlier the bond future bucked some traders' predictions of consolidation and climbed as high as 124.22 with a spurt in the Bund market providing the favourable backdrop.
Traders said the mood was still bullish with many looking for excuses to buy. Others said the view that domestic investors have plenty of cash to invest was supporting the market.
The 10-year spread, using the 6.50 percent 2006 OAT, narrowed slightly to three basis points from five on Monday.

One trader at a French bank said the pro-monetary union comments from the Franco-German summit had helped reinforce the feeling the two governments were committed to going ahead on time. Another trader at a French brokerage said the comments smacked more of political hype than anything substantive or new.

Sean Shepley, international economist at CS First Boston said "I'm not terribly excited by any of this, I suspect people are looking at the comments that strike them as supportive and which would justify the moves."
"Today (the officials) are going into convergence overload but there's not a lot in it," he said.

The December bond future slipped back as U.S. bonds fell, eventually settling at 124.06, up 20 centimes on the day. U.S. Treasuries fell after a Federal Reserve source said eight of 12 Fed banks submitted discount rate hike requests.
The short end of the curve remained supportive in France as continued franc strength bolstered hopes for a French intervention rate cut as soon as Thursday.

PIBOR contracts started the session well and traders said there were a number of large non-resident buyers at the open, covering short positions. The December contract reached a new contract high at 96.25 before slipping back to settle at 96.22.

Traders and analysts said a 10 basis point cut in the intervention rate, currently at 3.35 percent, was now being priced into interest rate futures and that the steepening of the curve was helping bring down long-term yields as well.
"The short end is leading things," said Shepley.
Some analysts said the Bank of France had room to move independently of the Bundesbank. Amar Douhane, analyst at Fimat said he expected a lowering of call money on Wednesday.
The franc broke through 3.40 during the morning and climbed as high as 3.3963 as stops were triggered in relatively light volume and the mark suffered against most European crosses.
The Treasury said it would sell 17 to 19 billion francs of 1998 and 2001 BTANs at auction on Thursday, slightly more than the total on offer last month.
